title: Equations of straight lines

points.text: Gradient, intercepts and the three common forms of a line
Parallel lines share a gradient; perpendicular gradients multiply to -1

bigPicture: A straight line is fixed by its gradient and one point. Lines are the simplest functions, and tangents and normals in calculus are built on them.

keyIdeas.cue: Name three forms of a line.
keyIdeas.answer: y = mx + c (gradient, y-intercept); ax + by + d = 0 (general); y − y1 = m(x − x1) (point-gradient).

keyIdeas.cue: Gradient rule for parallel and perpendicular lines?
keyIdeas.answer: Parallel: m1 = m2. Perpendicular: m1·m2 = −1, i.e. negative reciprocal.

keyTerms.def: change in y divided by change in x
where a line crosses an axis
